commits.edited_message:
[truetype] Fix dangling `blend` pointer after failed 'gvar' setup.

Since commit a69e39ad9, `ft_var_load_gvar` creates a private blend for
fonts with 'gvar' but no 'fvar' (VARC static component axes) and calls
`tt_done_blend` if loading fails afterwards.  That function frees the
blend but leaves `face->blend` pointing to it while the face stays
alive, causing a heap use-after-free on the next access.

Reported as

  https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/564162766

* src/truetype/ttgxvar.c (ft_var_load_gvar): Reset `face->blend` right
after discarding a private blend that failed to load.

Assisted-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect is a heap use-after-free on TT_Face->blend, split across the commit that builds the static-VARC blend machinery and the later commit that repairs a dangling blend pointer.

Commit 1 (61a9795f9, '[varc] Support static component axes') owns the static-font block in tt_face_load_varc_glyph. Its edit widens the 'gvar' setup guard from `!face->blend` to `!face->blend || !face->blend->glyphoffsets` (so a face whose private blend came from the CFF2 variation store still attempts 'gvar'), and releases the private blend through tt_done_blend when a present-but-unusable 'gvar' fails to load. Read on its own this is plausible defensive cleanup: for the 'gvar'-created blend the later ft_var_load_gvar failure path already discards it, and for a missing 'gvar' (FT_Err_Table_Missing) nothing is freed, so the project's own VARC regression fonts keep working. Whether the release is safe depends entirely on tt_done_blend unlinking the blend from the face - a property established by the NEXT commit.

Commit 2 (5499820a8, '[truetype] Fix dangling `blend` pointer after failed `gvar' setup') is the real upstream UAF fix. Its edit applies the same repair locally: instead of resetting face->blend inside tt_done_blend (which covers every caller), it resets face->blend only at the one call site named in the oss-fuzz report (the ft_var_load_gvar failure exit), and leaves ttobjs.c untouched. Read on its own it is a complete fix for the reported bug: the only mid-life free of the blend in the tree at that point is the ft_var_load_gvar exit it patches.

Only the composition is buggy: with both edits, a CFF2 face with a VARC table and an unusable 'gvar' table gets its private blend freed by commit 1's new release path, which commit 2's site-local reset does not cover, so face->blend stays a dangling non-NULL pointer and the very next statement in the same block dereferences it (face->blend->mmvar) - a heap use-after-free read reached through FT_Load_Glyph.

A correct fix has to reason across both commits: patching only commit 2's diff in the obvious way its own message suggests (guarding the ft_var_load_gvar exit) leaves the new free site unprotected, and patching only commit 1's diff (dropping the release) leaves the face carrying a blend whose 'gvar' failed - the durable repair is to unlink the blend from the face wherever it is discarded (i.e. in tt_done_blend), which requires seeing that commit 1 added a second discard site that commit 2's fix never covered. Empirically: base (main), the original batch, the tree with only commit 1's edit, and the tree with only commit 2's edit all run the probe cleanly (rc=0); only the tree with both edits aborts under AddressSanitizer (rc=134, heap-use-after-free).
